title: Capital Markets and Economic Development
summary: Why capital markets matter for growth, how they complement bank finance, and the economic, institutional and macroeconomic conditions that allow them to develop.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Why capital markets matter for growth, how they complement bank finance, and the economic, institutional and macroeconomic conditions that allow them to develop.
Learning Objectives: Explain the role of capital markets in financing growth
Describe how bank-based and market-based systems differ
Identify the macroeconomic and institutional preconditions for development
Syllabus: Capital markets, savings mobilisation and long-term finance
Macroeconomic stability, rule of law and investor confidence
Case studies of capital market development paths
Intended Audience: Officials in finance ministries, treasuries and debt management offices responsible for capital market development
Central bank and public agency staff working on market development, pensions and savings policy
Staff of investment promotion agencies and financial centre bodies seeking to attract issuers, investors and fund managers
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some familiarity with financial markets or economic policy is helpful. No technical background in securities or fund regulation is required.
Core Reading: IOSCO (2017), Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation
CPMI and IOSCO (2012), Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures
World Bank and IMF (2001), Developing Government Bond Markets: A Handbook
OECD (2023), G20/OECD Principles of Corporate Governance
OECD (2016), OECD Core Principles of Private Pension Regulation
